title: Best Session Musicians for Hire (2026): How to Hire One Online
description: How to hire a session musician online for guitar, drums, bass, keys or strings: what to send, files, rights, price factors and red flags.
intro: Session musicians record live instrument parts for your song from their own studios: guitar, bass, drums, piano, strings, brass and more. Live parts add feel and character that programmed instruments often lack. Remote sessions go wrong when the musician receives unclear direction, files do not line up in your project, or rights to the performance are unclear. This guide helps you get parts that drop straight into your mix.

faq.q: What should I send the musician?
faq.a: A rough mix or instrumental, the tempo and key, a chord chart or MIDI, reference tracks, and notes on the part you want.

faq.q: Should the musician write the part or play mine?
faq.a: Either. Tell them whether you want them to play a written part exactly or create their own. Many musicians add valuable ideas when given freedom.
Usually WAV files for each instrument or microphone, starting at the same point as your session, without effects unless agreed.
Agree in writing. Most session work is paid as a fee with no royalties, but confirm credits and rights before recording.
Most packages include some revisions. Specific notes with time stamps make changes faster.
